set.body:
EPIC -- STORY OUTPUT BUNDLE AND PURE-HTML/CSS VISUALIZATION SPEC.

Lodged at the owner's instruction from topic `story-output-format-and-visualization`. This records
BOARD CONSENSUS, not chief preference; where the board has not converged I say so rather than
pretend. Contributors: codex-story-output-format, codex-storyatlas-root, codex-storymodel4s-scout,
codex-storymodel-new-engineer, claude-storymodel4s-m1, alice.

OWNER'S REQUIREMENT, which fixes two things others were still weighing:
  "a proper, agreed upon plan for a spec for the output format -- BOTH A TEXT MARKUP AND A
   VISUALIZATION THAT IS PURE HTML/CSS AND CAN BE LOADED IN A BROWSER."
So: no JavaScript, no external resources, openable from the filesystem. That matches CodexHtml's
existing contract (no script, no external resource, no colour carries meaning) and makes it binding
rather than incidental.

=== AGREED (converged, multiple independent voices) ===

A1. THE OUTPUT IS A BUNDLE, NOT A FILE. Successful StoryModel semantics and the ACQUISITION ACCOUNT
    answer different questions. A provider failure must not become "no story" and must not become a
    clean empty graph. (scout, new-engineer, root)

A2. REUSE THE EXISTING CANONICAL `StoryModelCodec` ARTIFACT -- conventionally `storymodel.json`. Do
    NOT invent a parallel semantic JSON merely to make a bundle. The bundle adds manifest roles,
    sidecar/view/report receipts and optional loss records AROUND the existing interchange.
    (codex-story-output-format, adopted by root over their own earlier position)

A3. THREE TEXT IDENTITIES, NEVER COLLAPSED. root's original "Codex fragments equal the source
    exactly" was one claim doing three jobs; corrected to three laws:
      (i)   `source.txt` bytes EQUAL the original input bytes, with byte digest, declared charset
            and BOM/decoding disposition in the intake receipt;
      (ii)  concatenated Codex DOM text fragments EQUAL `StorySource.canonicalText` exactly, and
            every span resolves on that canonical zero-based half-open UTF-16 axis;
      (iii) the manifest binds original bytes, decoded raw string identity, canonical string
            identity and the canonicalization policy.
    THE PREVIEW MAY CLAIM EQUALITY WITH source.txt ONLY WHEN CANONICALIZATION IS PROVEN TO BE THE
    IDENTITY TRANSFORM. Raw-file fidelity and model-coordinate fidelity are both mandatory and are
    never silently treated as the same proof.

A4. TYPED UNIVERSE STATE, not an empty vector. `Established(ids, definitionIdentity) |
    Unestablished(reason)`. If planning or eligibility derivation itself fails, an empty vector would
    FALSELY ASSERT ZERO ELIGIBLE TARGETS. If Established, every id is accounted exactly once by a
    typed outcome; IF UNESTABLISHED, NO DOWNSTREAM ABSENCE OR COVERAGE RATE MAY BE COMPUTED, though
    the failure and receipt still render. (scout)

A5. THREE SEPARATE OUTCOMES INSIDE THE BUNDLE, not CLI exit codes:
      semantic:   Validated(modelRef) | Draft/Partial(gaps) | Refused(errors)
      per report: Produced(checksum) | Failed(receipt/error)
      invocation: exact source/input identity, configuration, attempts, completion disposition
    So a valid model with a failed HTML lowering is an AUDITABLE PARTIAL DELIVERY rather than a lost
    result, and a provider refusal produces an honest report WITHOUT MINTING A MODEL. (scout)

A6. ViewBasis DERIVES FROM ADMITTED PROVENANCE. `ResearcherReviewedFixture` cannot be a default on
    the general CLI path; acquired-silver, human-adjudicated and fixture bases are DIFFERENT
    AUTHORITY CLAIMS. (scout, new-engineer)

A7. D3 STANDS AND WAS EXTENDED RATHER THAN CONTESTED. Absence must be visible: a node with no
    evidence must not look like one with evidence; an imputed term must not render as measured; a
    cell whose support is 1.0 because nothing was ELIGIBLE must not look like one where everything
    was MEASURED. Nobody argued against it and scout carried it upstream as "the D3 denominator rule
    at the earliest stage".

=== NOT YET CONVERGED -- do not read agreement into these ===

O1. D1 standoff versus inline: I argued standoff and nobody contested it, but nobody explicitly
    affirmed it either. Absence of objection is not consensus. NEEDS ONE EXPLICIT ROUND.
O2. Whether the semantic JSON and the audit/result JSON are TWO FILES or ONE VERSIONED ENVELOPE.
    root calls this "wire design"; it is unresolved.
O3. D4, graph-over-text layout: whether a text rail with lane overlays suffices for causal and
    world-time relations that cross pages, or whether a second view is required. NOBODY HAS ANSWERED
    THIS and it is the hardest part.
O4. D5 round-trip versus report: implied by A2 (reusing StoryModelCodec makes the semantic half
    round-trippable) but the REPORT half's obligations are unstated.

=== SLICES, to become child beads once O1-O4 close ===
  S1  bundle manifest + the three text-identity laws (A3) with their courts
  S2  typed universe state and the denominator refusal (A4)
  S3  the three outcomes (A5) and the partial-delivery court
  S4  pure-HTML/CSS renderer contract (owner) extending CodexHtml's existing guarantees
  S5  declared-lossy external exporters
  S6  CLI input path -- bd-01M1998654XQRSNA6R16S2ABDQ, blocked on Stage 1b

BLOCKED ON: Stage 1b (bd-01M17MET0E4TWW304YKXPHBSBG, 4 of 50 sentences) for anything that must
consume arbitrary ASCII. S1-S5 are specification work and are NOT blocked by it.

NO IMPLEMENTATION IS AUTHORIZED BY THIS EPIC. It records what the board agreed and what it did not.
set.title: EPIC: story output bundle + pure-HTML/CSS visualization spec (board consensus)
